children: Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices fell on Monday morning due to lower demand from power plants and an expected uptick in Norwegian exports when an outage at the Troll field ends.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was down €0.94 to €90.01 euros per megawatt hour (MWh) by 0826 GMT, ICE data showed.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) fell by 2.26 pence to 224.75 pence per therm.

Two oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz that led to explosions, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Monday, after six tankers caught fire in similar incidents on Sunday and Monday. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

Wind speeds are forecast above normal this week, reducing gas-for-power demand. Norwegian exports are forecast to rise on the day ahead to 337 million cubic metres per day as an outage at the Troll field is expected to end tomorrow, LSEG data showed.
North-west Europe local distribution zone demand, which includes home heating, is expected to rise next week as average temperatures are revised 1.7 degrees Celsius lower to 4.9C.

North-west Europe gas stocks are at 345 terawatt (TWh) hours today, well below the 446 TWh a year ago, and are forecast to reach 237 TWh by December 30 against 317 TWh a year earlier, said LSEG gas analyst Saku Jussila.

Analysts at HSBC said Europe's gas inventories could end the refill season this winter at 20% full, which would be the second lowest on record. Inventories could reach 28% full in the case of milder weather and colder weather could result in 12% full storage.

HSBC said Europe's first so-called "dunkelflaute"- a prolonged period with little to no wind and minimal sunlight - saw surge in gas-fired power demand and the acceleration in storage withdrawals. Further "dunkelflaute" episodes, coupled with colder weather, could drastically strain Europe’s gas balances and drive sharp price increases.

"LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz could be curbed further, with potential geopolitical escalations in the region. New LNG facilities ramping up/starting up remain at risk of being delayed. Unplanned outages at other LNG facilities, or with Norwegian pipeline deliveries, can easily put additional stress on gas balances. With around 4.5 months of the winter season remaining, we see a lot of factors that could go wrong," the analysts said.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
edged down by €0.06 at €88.09 per metric ton.
